From procurement bots to

The current product is an AI copilot for manual assembly. A camera sits over the workbench and watches the operator's hands. Computer vision reads the motion, compares it against the correct sequence, and flags a deviation in real time - before the unit moves on. The company's own line for it is plain: "Ship faster than ever, error-free."
The company's framing of the product
The mascot is a flame that never quite stops being a robot - two eyes and a pair of antennae hiding in the base. Fitting for a product whose whole job is to keep watching.
LumiBot doesn't sell a shrink-wrapped box. Onboarding runs in three phases, and each one lowers the risk of the next.
The onboarding pipeline
Live in production, catching errors in real time.
Continuous improvement as the model sees more work.
From spreadsheets to hands

The through-line from then to now is productivity, not a particular technology. The company moved from automating the paperwork around manufacturing to watching the manufacturing itself. Same north star, different medium - spreadsheets gave way to a camera pointed at a workbench.

Before this, he consulted at McKinsey, IBM and Honeywell, and co-founded STOQO - a fresh-produce supply startup that, at its height, served roughly 40,000 restaurants with a workforce around 1,500 and about USD 13M raised. He studied computer science and chemical engineering at UNSW, then added an MBA across London Business School and MIT.

That resume reads like the setup for exactly this product: enterprise consulting taught him where industrial pain lives, and running a high-volume physical-goods operation taught him what a single error costs when it multiplies across a line.

Beyond Y Combinator, LumiBot's early-stage backing includes Monk's Hill Ventures, Alpha JWC Ventures, Goodwater Capital, SWC Global and January Capital - a lineup that reads distinctly Southeast Asia, matching the company's Singapore base and regional roots. The thesis they're buying is human-plus-AI industrial productivity, delivered without asking a factory to rebuild anything.
High-Precision Perception Ensures Crisp Data at the Source

On the data front, LumiBot has fully operationalized its real-robot teleoperation collection pipeline for continuous data gathering. Simultaneously, its egocentric (Ego) data-to-robot mapping scheme has achieved millimeter-level precision verification, providing stable training inputs.

Currently, LumiBot is advancing scenario validation and technical verification (POCs) with industry leaders across automotive manufacturing, 3C electronics, and life sciences, systematically proving the scale-up capability and reliability of its hardware and systems in actual production environments.
